rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a very poor-quality early/failed blastulating embryo and absent/degenerate ICM/TE, but it overstates some image-specific details such as uniform zona, visible debris/fragmentation, and confidently calling arrest when the image alone supports severe delay/poor blastulation more than definitive arrest.

Integrates age, low AMH, limited oocyte yield, normal sperm, tubal factor, BMI, and endometrium well, and appropriately identifies embryo quality as the dominant prognostic factor; some links (e.g., former smoking as explanatory for DOR) are somewhat speculative.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent, with prognosis driven primarily by the 0DD embryo grade and modified by age/reserve/endometrium. Minor overreach appears in assigning mechanisms like genomic activation failure and precise live-birth implications from morphology alone.

Use of Gardner grading and emphasis on poor prognosis are aligned, but several recommendations (routine estradiol addition, growth hormone, DHEA, melatonin, and strong endorsement of adjuncts) are not firmly guideline-supported and are presented more positively than current evidence warrants.

Provides clear counseling points and practical future-cycle options such as protocol review, possible Day 3 transfer with low embryo numbers, embryo banking discussion, and donor-oocyte counseling. Some suggestions are useful but should be framed more cautiously given limited evidence.
